chains.title: GABPA gains an alt-specific TERT promoter site and activates TERT in glioblastoma

links.claim: GABPA binds the alt A allele more strongly than the ref G allele because C250T creates a de novo ETS/GABP motif. GABPA is chosen as the canonical ETS-family DNA-binding subunit recruited by TERT promoter mutations; no QBiC-SELEX model is given here, so this is motif- and literature-based and requires occupancy testing.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter and alters a cis-regulatory ETS/GABP motif.
Glioblastoma cells commonly carry TERT promoter mutations and express TERT.
Increased TERT transcription and telomerase activity support immortalization and tumor maintenance, contributing to glioblastoma.

predictions: GABPA ChIP enriches the alt A allele over ref G at chr5:1295135 in a heterozygous glioblastoma line.
The alt allele increases TERT reporter expression, and GABPA knockdown reduces this alt-specific increase.
TERT expression is higher in glioblastoma lines carrying C250T than in ref lines, other things being equal.
falsified_if: GABPA shows no allele-specific occupancy at the variant in heterozygous glioblastoma cells.
The alt allele does not increase TERT reporter activity, or GABPA knockdown does not reduce any alt-specific effect.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated allelic effect from C250T
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy is detected at chr5:1295135.
Ref G and alt A TERT promoter reporters behave equivalently in the relevant cell type.
Any disease association is explained by a linked causal variant, passenger mutation at a recurrent TERT promoter hotspot, or no allelic effect.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GABPA or another ETS-factor occupancy is demonstrated at the variant and paired with an allelic TERT expression effect.

chains.title: ETS1 gains an alt-specific site and activates TERT in glioblastoma

links.claim: ETS1 binds the alt A allele more strongly than the ref G allele through the ETS motif created by C250T. ETS1 shares ETS-family specificity with GABPA; no QBiC-SELEX model is given for ETS1 here, so this is weaker than the GABPA explanation and needs occupancy evidence.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter and creates a candidate ETS1-binding site.
Glioblastoma cells express ETS-family factors and express TERT.
ETS1-driven TERT activation increases telomerase activity and supports tumor maintenance in glioblastoma.

predictions: ETS1 ChIP enriches the alt A allele over ref G at the variant, while GABPA does not.
ETS1 knockdown, not GABPA knockdown, reduces the alt-specific TERT reporter increase.
falsified_if: ETS1 shows no allele-specific occupancy at the variant.
GABPA, rather than ETS1, is the ETS factor whose knockdown reverses the alt-specific TERT increase.

chains.title: GABPA binds the alt allele but does not activate TERT in glioblastoma

links.claim: GABPA binds the alt A allele more strongly than ref G, but this binding may be repressive or context-dependent rather than activating. No QBiC-SELEX model is given, so the direction is motif-based and requires occupancy and functional testing.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter and alters a GABPA-binding ETS motif.
The element is in the TERT promoter, but the allelic effect on TERT transcription is not necessarily activating.
Glioblastoma cells can have TERT promoter mutations without a simple proportional increase in TERT from the mutant allele.
Any disease contribution would not be through increased TERT activation from this allele, or would require additional context.

predictions: GABPA ChIP enriches the alt A allele, but the alt allele does not increase TERT reporter expression.
GABPA knockdown does not reduce TERT expression in C250T-heterozygous glioblastoma cells, or increases it.
falsified_if: The alt allele increases TERT reporter activity and GABPA knockdown specifically reduces that increase.

matrix.test: Allele-specific ChIP-qPCR for GABPA and ETS1 at chr5:1295135, with TERT expression readout, in a heterozygous glioblastoma line

outcomes.outcome: GABPA enriches the alt A allele over ref G, and TERT expression is higher from the alt allele.
ETS1 enriches the alt A allele over ref G, while GABPA does not, and TERT expression is higher from the alt allele.
GABPA enriches the alt A allele, but TERT expression is not higher from the alt allele.
Neither GABPA nor ETS1 shows allele-specific occupancy, and there is no allelic TERT expression difference.

matrix.test: TERT promoter luciferase reporter with ref G versus alt A, plus GABPA or ETS1 knockdown, in glioblastoma cells

outcomes.outcome: Alt increases reporter activity, and GABPA knockdown reduces the alt-specific increase.
Alt increases reporter activity, and ETS1 knockdown reduces the alt-specific increase, while GABPA knockdown does not.
Alt does not increase reporter activity despite GABPA occupancy.
Ref and alt reporters are equivalent.

matrix.test: Reanalyze existing glioblastoma ChIP-seq/ATAC data for GABPA and ETS1 occupancy over the TERT promoter variant

outcomes.outcome: A GABPA occupancy peak overlaps the variant.
An ETS1 occupancy peak overlaps the variant without a GABPA peak.
No relevant TF occupancy or open-chromatin signal overlaps the variant.

next_experiment: Allele-specific ChIP-qPCR for GABPA and ETS1 at chr5:1295135 in a heterozygous glioblastoma line, with a TERT expression readout; this is the cheapest direct test separating the GABPA and ETS1 chains.
